verdict.rationale: Aleph's own documentation names headcount planning backed by live HRIS, ATS, ERP, and spreadsheet data, and separately mentions versioned forecasts. That establishes a first-party headcount planning capability, but the evidence is a single thin line with no detail on how it works. Missing for 10: role-level planning granularity, explicit linkage to payroll actuals, documented flow of planned hires into the expense forecast, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, I can plan headcount at the role level, tied to payroll actuals, with planned hires flowing into the expense forecast

citations.quote: Headcount planning backed by live HRIS, ATS, ERP, and spreadsheet data.
Versioned forecasts, scenario modeling, and board-ready variance analysis.
